Subject: Increasing completion times + occasional 503s - urgent

Hi Marissa,

We're seeing intermittent but impactful slow completions on our checkout LLM calls since last night (~Nov 26 21:30 PST). The bulk of requests complete under 600ms, but about ~0.7% of requests spike between 6s-18s and we've had a handful of 503s and 429s during peak retries. This is hitting our web checkout flow and causing user friction — conversions are down ~4% for the last 2 hours.

Sample request IDs: nimbus-req-20281127-9a1, nimbus-req-20281127-9a2, nimbus-req-20281127-9b0.

I've attached screenshots and a small trace export (nimbus-tail-trace.zip). Our engineering team can provide more traces if you need them. Can you escalate? We are on a tight campaign and this needs executive attention if it continues.

Thanks,
Chris
Director of Engineering
NimbusPay

From: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai

Date: Tue, 27 Nov 2028 09:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Increasing completion times + occasional 503s - urgent

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Mapped the sample request IDs: all hit our hosted inference tier initially and then were routed to a small set of Dedicated spillover nodes in us-west-2 during peak.
- Observed intermittent queue depth spikes on a handful of GPUs with concurrent KV cache eviction events. When the KV cache misses occur, subsequent token generation paths show execution times of up to ~16s for long prompts.
- We also saw transient 503s originating from an internal circuit-breaker tied to per-customer concurrency caps. The circuit opens when the per-customer inflight count temporarily exceeds configured caps + a backlog threshold.

Immediate next steps I’m running now:
1) Pull detailed per-node traces for the request IDs (pushing trace-snippet.txt to this thread).
2) Temporarily disable the tight concurrency cap for NimbusPay on the spillover pool and monitor concurrency.
3) Reduce batching window for their route from 50ms -> 20ms to limit head-of-line blocking for small, latency-sensitive calls.

Risk notes: disabling the cap and reducing batching window will increase unit cost and could reduce throughput efficiency elsewhere. I will limit the change to NimbusPay’s route only.

Vivek
Senior SRE, Runtime Reliability

From: hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Nov 2028 10:30:00 -0800
Subject: Action plan: NimbusPay — emergency mitigations and rollback plan

Team — reading Vivek's findings and Chris's traces. Proposed action plan (execute immediately upon Marcus/exec sign-off):

1) Emergency route override: bump NimbusPay per-customer concurrency cap from 60 -> 140 on the Dedicated spillover pool (us-west-2) for the next 6 hours.
2) Shorten batching window for that route 50ms -> 20ms and add a temporary bypass for requests tagged latency_sensitive=true.
3) Increase KV cache TTL for their hot-prefixes to avoid repeated cache thrash; backfill hot keys where traces show misses.
4) Enable verbose slow-path logging for sampled requests (1/1000) and ship to the incident bucket.
5) Post-incident: run an RCA focused on: batching interactions, prefix cache eviction pattern, and routing fallback heuristics.

Risks and mitigations:
- Capacity impact: will consume reserved headroom; recommend notifying sales/finance and logging costs to DEAL-8421.
- Other customers: changes scoped by route to limit blast radius, but there is some cross-pool interference risk — Ops will closely monitor throttle metrics and fail open if necessary.

Ask: Markus, can you approve the temporary override so we can proceed now? I’ll coordinate rollbacks after the window.

Hannah
Director, Platform Operations
hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
